newsitem.title: HONG KONG: GITIC Enterprises shares rocket 352 pct in HK.
newsitem.headline: GITIC Enterprises shares rocket 352 pct in HK.

text.p: Small issue size, strong subscription response and hopes for future asset injections combined to give shares in GITIC Enterprises Ltd an explosive debut on the Hong Kong bourse on Wednesday, brokers said.
Shares of the construction materials and property concern finished the morning session at HK$4.75 (61 U.S. cents), up 352 percent from their issue price of HK$1.05.
The shares, which topped the list of most actively traded stocks in value terms, hit a high of HK$5.15 after debuting at HK$4.50. Their low was HK$4.25.
Volume was 115.77 million shares worth HK$538.22 million.
"The performance was stronger than we generally expected," said Ben Kwong, research director at Dharmala Securities.
Analysts said many investors who failed to subscribe for the shares during their initial public offering (IPO) were seen rushing in to buy.
The relatively small issue size and high subscription level had made the issue particularly hot, they said.

"Anticipation of room on the upside on hopes of future asset injections (by its China-based parent) also fueled follow-through buying," Kwong said. "However, the shares were seen capped at their high of HK$5.15 after the sharp rally."
GITIC Enterprises imports and sells construction materials in Hong Kong and China, and also owns the second floor of a shopping mall at GITIC Plaza in Guangzhou.

The company is indirectly controlled by the Guangdong provincial goverment's investment arm, Guangdong International Trust and Investment Corp (GITIC), which had total assets of about 20.56 billion yuan as at the end of 1995.

GITIC Enterprises offered 100 million new shares at HK$1.05 each in its IPO, of which the 90 million shares available for public subscription was 892 times subscribed -- Hong Kong's most popular-ever IPO in term of subscription level.
That broke the record carmaker Denway Investment Ltd made in February 1993. Its 330 million-share issue was 657 times oversubscribed.

"The strong earnings outlook after taking into account an expected huge exceptional gain due to interest income from the subscription monies also gave investors a positive sign to buy," said Henri Lui, analyst at Mansion House.
Analysts estimated the interest income would be over HK$40 million, almost equal to the company's own earnings forecast of over HK$41 million for the year ended in December 1996.

"Its earnings outlook is also seen bright on expectation of increasing demand for granite and marble products from the local office and hotel property developments," Lui said. "There are not many suppliers of these kinds of materials in Hong Kong."
Analysts said the next move of the stock would depend on the company's asset injection plans.
